sense: trust that someone or something will not fail
also: I’m sure it will be fine

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, semi-deponent: with an accusative and infinitive (“I’m confident that”), or with the dative or ablative (“trust in”)
evidence: Ter. Haut. 160: Salvum affutūrum esse hīc cōnfīdō propediem.
terms.comment: In speech Latin says the verb: cōnfīdō is a firm hope, stronger than spērō (Cic. Att. 6.9.1, Lewis & Short). For relying on someone, see depend.

terms.grammar: noun, first declension: with the genitive of what one trusts
evidence: Caes. BC 2.37.1 (Lewis & Short): tantam habēbat suārum rērum fīdūciam
terms.comment: The noun: trust in a person, a thing or a plan; fīdūcia suī is self-confidence (see self-confidence). In law it is also a pledge held in trust (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Salvum affutūrum esse hīc cōnfīdō propediem.
phrases.english: I’m confident he’ll be back here safe and sound any day now.

phrases.latin: dē Atticā molestum, sed quoniam leviter, rēctē esse cōnfīdō.
phrases.english: Too bad about Attica, but since it’s mild, I’m confident she’ll be fine.

phrases.latin: quī reliquiās hujus bellī oppresserit, eum tōtīus bellī cōnfectōrem fore; quem tē et optō esse et cōnfīdō futūrum.
phrases.english: whoever crushes what is left of this war will be the one who ends the whole war; and that is what I hope you are, and am confident you will be.
